supporting_cases.relevance: Closest award comparator because it combines damp and mould, broader property repairs, doors/windows/roof-related works, complaint handling, apology and repair-update orders.

supporting_cases.quote: Maladministration in the landlord’s handling of the resident’s reports of repairs at the property, including damp and mould. Service failure in the landlord’s complaint handling.
supporting_cases.relevance: Supports the likely liability split: substantive repairs maladministration with complaint handling service failure.

supporting_cases.quote: The landlord did not inspect the property after the resident’s January 2022 report of mould until September 2022, approximately 7 months later. This meant an approximate 7-month delay, which fell significantly outside its repair standards.
supporting_cases.relevance: Shows that substantial delay in investigating damp and mould is treated as maladministration, especially where the issue is serious or recurring.

supporting_cases.quote: The landlord did not keep proper oversight of the repairs or adequately communicate with the resident. These failings contributed to delays in completing repairs and had a significant impact on the resident. The landlord recognised this and offered compensation which was enough to put things right.
supporting_cases.relevance: Useful counter-comparator: similar repair and communication failings may be reasonable redress where the landlord has already made a proportionate offer.
